stocks.name: Apple
stocks.summary: Apple is up modestly today (+0.2%) and has rallied 9.1% over the month, sitting 2.0% below its 52‑week high and still 41.2% above its low. The stock remains near the top of its range, so investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for signs of sustained momentum.

stocks.name: Microsoft
stocks.summary: Microsoft gained 2.0% on the day and is 6.0% under its 52‑week peak, still 43.5% above its low. With steady weekly and monthly gains, the next catalyst is the company's cloud spending outlook in its upcoming earnings report.

stocks.name: NVIDIA
stocks.summary: NVIDIA slipped 3.4% on the day, extending a 6‑week decline and now sits 10.3% below its 52‑week high, though still 28% above its low. The key watch is whether the recent pullback stabilizes ahead of the next earnings release and AI demand updates.

stocks.name: Alphabet
stocks.summary: Alphabet rose 3.2% today, trading 13.1% under its 52‑week high and 48.1% above its low. The stock is recovering from a dip, so investors should focus on ad‑revenue trends and any guidance on AI monetization coming next quarter.

stocks.name: Amazon
stocks.summary: Amazon fell 1.3% on the day, remaining 10.7% below its 52‑week high and 27.5% above its low after a modest monthly decline. Attention should turn to retail sales data and cloud growth forecasts ahead of earnings.

stocks.name: Meta Platforms
stocks.summary: Meta climbed 2.7% today, trading 14.4% below its 52‑week high and 26.7% above its low after strong weekly and monthly gains. Investors should monitor user growth metrics and the rollout of AI features for the next catalyst.

stocks.name: Tesla
stocks.summary: Tesla slipped 1.8% on the day but is up 5.6% over the month, still 26.7% under its 52‑week high yet 20.3% above its low. The next focus is production and delivery numbers, especially any updates on new model rollouts.

stocks.name: Broadcom
stocks.summary: Broadcom dropped 4.8% today, now 28.3% below its 52‑week high and 17.7% above its low after a sharp monthly decline. Watch for the upcoming earnings beat and guidance on its semiconductor and infrastructure segments.

stocks.name: Advanced Micro Devices
stocks.summary: AMD fell 4.4% on the day but remains near the top of a massive rally, 15.1% under its 52‑week high and up 213.5% from its low, with YTD gains of 120.8%. The key watch is the next earnings report and its competitive positioning versus Nvidia.

stocks.name: Oracle
stocks.summary: Oracle has slipped 3.7% on the day and is down 8.8% week‑to‑date, sitting 55.4% below its 52‑week high and still 25.9% above its low, indicating a prolonged downtrend. The key watch is whether the recent earnings beat or cloud‑computing guidance can halt the slide.

stocks.name: Salesforce
stocks.summary: Salesforce rallied 4.7% intraday, now just 2.1% shy of its 52‑week peak after a 28.8% monthly gain, showing strong upside from its low base. Investors should focus on the next product‑revenue update and integration progress of recent acquisitions.

stocks.name: JPMorgan Chase
stocks.summary: JPMorgan fell 1.7% today, trading 4.1% below its 52‑week high but still 25% above its low, reflecting modest volatility amid a 9.1% YTD gain. The next catalyst is the bank’s upcoming earnings and any shift in net interest margin expectations.

stocks.name: Bank of America
stocks.summary: Bank of America dropped 5.1% on the day, now 7.8% under its 52‑week high while remaining 28.6% above its low, extending a broader sector pullback. Watch for the bank’s loan‑growth figures and Fed rate outlook ahead of its earnings release.

stocks.name: Visa
stocks.summary: Visa edged up 1.3% and is trading 2.3% below its 52‑week high, still 27.5% above its low, indicating resilience in a high‑growth range. The next focus is transaction‑volume trends and any pricing‑power updates in its quarterly report.

stocks.name: Mastercard
stocks.summary: Mastercard gained 0.9% but sits 4.2% under its 52‑week high and 22% above its low, showing modest upside in a stable range. Investors should monitor cross‑border spend recovery and the upcoming earnings guidance.

stocks.name: Netflix
stocks.summary: Netflix rose 3.8% on the day, now 35.3% below its 52‑week high yet 18.8% above its low, suggesting a tentative rebound after a weak YTD. The key metric to watch is subscriber growth in the next earnings beat.

stocks.name: Eli Lilly
stocks.summary: Eli Lilly climbed 2.0% and remains 11.1% under its 52‑week high while up 60.3% from its low, reflecting strong momentum on new product launches. Watch upcoming FDA decisions and Q3 sales guidance for the next move.

stocks.name: UnitedHealth
stocks.summary: UnitedHealth rose 1.8% and is 11.6% below its 52‑week high, still 49.8% above its low, maintaining a solid YTD gain. The next inflection point is its Medicare Advantage enrollment trends and earnings outlook.

stocks.name: Johnson & Johnson
stocks.summary: Johnson & Johnson is up modestly today (+0.3%) and sits about 4.3% below its 52‑week high while still 56.4% above its low, reflecting a solid YTD gain of 30.5%. The recent bounce after a 3.2% weekly dip suggests resilience, but investors should watch upcoming earnings guidance for any shifts in its pharma pipeline.

stocks.name: Walmart
stocks.summary: Walmart rose 1.8% on the day, trading 18.5% under its 52‑week high and 9.3% above its low, with YTD performance slightly negative at -2.6%. The stock’s recent pullback over the month points to pricing pressure, so the key watch is same‑store sales trends in the next quarterly report.

stocks.name: Costco
stocks.summary: Costco gained 1.6% intraday, now 15.9% below its 52‑week peak and 8.6% above its low, delivering an 8.0% YTD rise. Momentum remains modest after a 4.5% monthly decline; investors should focus on membership renewal rates and any changes in discretionary spending.

stocks.name: Home Depot
stocks.summary: Home Depot edged up 0.7% but remains 24.4% off its 52‑week high and only 6.1% above its low, with an 8.2% YTD decline. The recent 8.4% monthly slide highlights sensitivity to housing market trends, making upcoming builder‑confidence data a critical catalyst.

stocks.name: Exxon Mobil
stocks.summary: Exxon Mobil slipped 0.5% today, trading 2.4% below its 52‑week high yet 53.5% above its low, buoyed by a strong 37.3% YTD gain. With oil prices volatile, the next driver will be OPEC production decisions and the company’s quarterly capital‑expenditure outlook.

stocks.name: Coca-Cola
stocks.summary: Coca‑Cola rose 1.2% on the session, now 2.9% under its 52‑week high and 38.8% above its low, posting a robust 31.0% YTD increase. Investors should keep an eye on global volume trends and any pricing adjustments in emerging markets.

stocks.name: Walt Disney
stocks.summary: Disney advanced 1.9% today, sitting 5.6% below its 52‑week high and 18.4% above its low, with YTD performance marginally down at -2.2%. The key focus is the rollout of its streaming strategy and the upcoming earnings beat‑and‑guide for the parks segment.
